title: See a counter wrap
modelNote: This is a {width}-bit teaching model. The lesson uses {realWidth}-bit registers.
instruction: Choose Advance one tick. Each tick adds one. Watch which bits the counter stores.
initialNote: No tick has advanced yet. There is no completed addition to show.
initialStatus: Starting reading: {stored}. No ticks have passed.
stepStatus: Ticks passed: {ticks}. Stored reading: {stored}. Last tick's full sum: {fullSum}. Carry out: {carryOut}.
limitNote: This example ends after {maximumTicks} ticks. Choose Reset to try it again.
carryExplanation: Carry out is the bit beyond the counter's width. It is separate from the bits stored in the counter.
wrapExplanation: The full sum is {fullSum}, or {fullPattern} in binary. The counter stores only the low bits: {pattern}, read as {stored}. This is unsigned wrap.
elapsedTitle: Count the ticks across the wrap
elapsedExplanation: The earlier reading is {start}; the later reading is {stored}. Subtract the earlier reading from the later one and keep the low {width} bits. The result is {elapsed}, matching the ticks you advanced.
elapsedAssumption: This measures elapsed ticks only if the counter advances normally and fewer than {range} ticks pass between readings.
turnLimit: The two readings alone cannot tell you how many complete turns the counter made.
architectureNote: RISC-V has no carry or signed-overflow flag. The carry shown here belongs to the four-bit calculation.
